speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; please tell me, have you noticed any other specific symptoms like joint pain, a red ring on your palms or soles, or a sore throat?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a pruritic lacy rash on the trunk and extremities, combined with recent viral prodrome symptoms, is classic for this condition. No further testing or questions are required to confirm this diagnosis.
